title: Regularity and regular morphisms on quasi-excellent formal charts
statement: A Noetherian adic formal scheme means a ringed space with a finite cover by $\operatorname{Spf}A$, where $A$ is a commutative Noetherian ring complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal $K$; its points are the primes containing $K$ and its structure sheaf is the inverse limit of the structure sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}(A/K^n)$. A coherent formal ideal is an ideal subsheaf locally associated to a finite ideal of such an $A$ by completed localization. An open ideal contains a power of the ideal of definition. Work over $\mathbf Q$ and assume the chart rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A formal scheme is reduced, respectively regular, if its complete affine chart rings are reduced, respectively regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. On $\operatorname{Spf}A$, the singular ideal is the radical ideal defining the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. These notions are independent of the affine cover: reducedness and regularity can be checked on any formal open cover, and the singular ideals restrict compatibly and glue to a coherent ideal. Quasi-excellence is likewise independent of the cover. For every formal affine open $\operatorname{Spf}B\subseteq\mathfrak X$ contained in a formal affine $\operatorname{Spf}A$, the restriction map $A\to B$ is regular. A morphism $h:\mathfrak Y\to\mathfrak X$ between these formal schemes is regular if it admits formal affine covers on which its ring maps are flat with Noetherian geometrically regular residue-field fibres [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. For every pair of formal affine opens $V\subseteq\mathfrak Y$, $U\subseteq\mathfrak X$ with $h(V)\subseteq U$, the induced ring map is then regular; regularity is local on source and target. Open immersions, finite disjoint unions of regular morphisms, and composites of regular morphisms are regular. For a reduced formal pair $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak K)$ with invertible ideal of definition locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, if its singular ideal contains a power of $\mathfrak K$, then each formal open subpair has these same properties. If its reduced closed fibre is of finite type over a characteristic-zero field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], this holds for each quasi-compact formal open as well.

source.place: Temkin §2.4.3, §2.4.9 and Lemma 2.4.6 with its proof (printed pp.14–17); §§3.1.1 and 3.1.4 for the open subpairs. Quasi-excellence is essential for formal localization regularity; these assertions are not claimed for arbitrary Noetherian formal schemes. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Check quasi-excellence from any cover by quasi-excellent formal affines. In another chart $\operatorname{Spf}B$, with ideal of definition $K$, take common principal neighbourhoods with the original charts using [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement]. Each ring $C=B_{\{b\}}$ is quasi-excellent by the last assertion of [lem-per-quasi-excellent-formal-affines], applied to the original complete chart ring (its completion is itself). The quotient $C/KC$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and a G-ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring]. It is J-2: a finite list generating an algebra over this quotient also generates it over $C$, so use J-2 for $C$ in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute, lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $C/KC=(B/K)_b$. These ordinary principal opens cover $\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$, the underlying space of the formal chart.

source.place: §2.4.3: reduction to a cover of the ordinary closed fibre

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] and [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] to the Step-1 cover of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$. Its coordinate ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], hence this scheme is locally Noetherian. The two criteria give G-ring and J-2 for $B/K$, hence quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Now [lem-per-gabber-adic-quasi-excellence] applies to the Noetherian $K$-adically complete ring $B$ and proves it quasi-excellent. Thus all formal affine charts have quasi-excellent rings regardless of the initial covering. The same ordinary affine-cover criteria show that every ordinary affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has quasi-excellent ring whenever $A$ is quasi-excellent.

source.place: §2.4.3, Gabber completion criterion and ordinary affine locality

proof.text: For a quasi-excellent complete chart $A$, apply [lem-per-regular-morphism-formal-completion] to the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, completing both sides along its ideal of definition. Step 2 supplies quasi-excellence on ordinary affines. The identity is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], and each fibre and its finite field extensions are fields, hence regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The ideal is coherent: it is a finite ideal on a Noetherian affine, so use [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The completion is $\operatorname{Spf}A$. The cited theorem applied to the whole target chart and any source formal affine open gives regularity of its restriction $A\to B$. More generally, if a covering chart map $A\to B$ is regular, apply the same theorem to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. For each residue-field fibre, [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] turns the purely-inseparable test in the regular-ring-map definition into regularity after every finite field extension. Thus the ring hypotheses give scheme flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] (a flat ring map induces a flat morphism of spectra) and regular geometric fibres by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Both schemes are Noetherian and quasi-excellent on every affine by Step 2. Continuity lets us replace the ideal of definition of $A$ by a power whose image lies in the chosen ideal of definition of $B$; powers give the same completions. The theorem therefore proves regularity on any compatible formal affine subpair inside these covering charts. No finite type or adicity assumption on the morphism is needed.

Suppose $h$ has regular chart maps on a cover. Fix arbitrary compatible charts $\operatorname{Spf}E,\operatorname{Spf}F$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $F$. By [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement], it is a formal point. Choose a covering pair containing it and its image. Take a common principal target neighbourhood $W$ inside both target charts, then a common principal source neighbourhood $T$ inside both source charts and $h^{-1}W$. Their rings are $E_{\{a\}}$ and $F_{\{b\}}$. Step 3 gives regularity of $E_{\{a\}}\to F_{\{b\}}$ and $E\to E_{\{a\}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] the composite is regular; its fibres are localizations of quotients of a Noetherian ring, by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The refinement lemma supplies $\mathfrak n$ above $\mathfrak m$ and a faithfully flat $F_{\mathfrak m}\to(F_{\{b\}})_{\mathfrak n}$. Set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m\cap E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal], $E_{\mathfrak p}\to(F_{\{b\}})_{\mathfrak n}$ is regular, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence] descends it to $E_{\mathfrak p}\to F_{\mathfrak m}$. The same maximal-ideal criterion gives regularity of $E\to F$. This proves the assertion on every affine pair and locality in both source and target.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.6, second paragraph, faithful-flat descent at maximal ideals

proof.text: Reducedness ascends along chart restrictions by Step 3 and [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target]. Conversely, if an open cover has reduced chart rings, a nilpotent section on another affine chart restricts to zero on its intersections with covering charts (cover these intersections by smaller formal affines), and is zero by the sheaf axiom. Regularity ascends along restrictions by Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent]; geometric regularity gives its regular-fibre hypothesis by the trivial field extension. Conversely, at a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of another chart $B$, choose a common principal neighbourhood inside a regular covering chart. Its ring $C$ is regular by ascent. The refinement lemma gives a faithfully flat local map $B_{\mathfrak m}\to C_{\mathfrak n}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] gives regularity of $B_{\mathfrak m}$. Every prime of $B$ lies below a maximal ideal, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] gives regularity of every $B_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus $B$ is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This proves cover-independence of both notions.

source.place: §2.4.9, ascent and descent across completed localizations

proof.text: For a restriction $A\to B$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$, set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. Its local map is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal]. Flatness and its regular closed fibre imply that $A_{\mathfrak p}$ regular entails $B_{\mathfrak q}$ regular by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre]. The converse follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular]. Thus the nonregular locus upstairs is exactly the inverse image of the nonregular locus downstairs. Each is closed by J-2 in [def-exc-excellent-ring] applied to the ring itself. Let $J_A,J_B$ be their radical defining ideals. Base change of $A\to B$ along the finite type quotient $A\to A/J_A$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change], and its target is $B/J_AB$. Because $A/J_A$ is reduced, [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target] makes $B/J_AB$ reduced; these quotient rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. Hence $J_AB$ is radical. Its vanishing set is the nonregular locus of $B$ by the local equivalence above. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] it equals $J_B$.

Each $J_A$ is finite because $A$ is Noetherian. On a formal principal open with ring $C=\widehat{A_a}$, restrict the associated completed ideal of $J_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] applied to $0\to(J_A)_a\to A_a\to(A/J_A)_a\to0$, this is an ideal in $C$. Its image is $J_AC$: complete a finite presentation $A_a^r\twoheadrightarrow(J_A)_a$ and apply the same exactness to get a surjection $C^r\twoheadrightarrow\widehat{(J_A)_a}$; its composite into $C$ is the map given by the generators of $J_A$. Step 6 identifies this image with $J_C$. Common principal neighbourhoods [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] therefore identify the chart ideal subsheaves on every intersection. Define the global ideal by those sections whose restrictions to the charts lie in these ideals. The sheaf axiom gives its uniqueness and the prescribed restrictions. It is coherent in the formal sense of the statement, since it is locally associated to the finite ideal $J_A$. This proves compatibility of actual ideals as well as their zero sets.

source.place: §2.4.9; Stacks 00MB, lemma-completion-flat, exactness on finite modules

proof.text: An open immersion is locally a restriction inside an affine chart, hence regular by Steps 3--4. A finite disjoint union of regular morphisms has regular ring maps on the union of their covering pairs, so satisfies the definition. For a composite choose successive compatible affine neighbourhoods around each source point. Step 4 makes both corresponding ring maps regular, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] makes their composite regular: its fibres are localizations of quotients of its Noetherian target by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Such neighbourhoods cover, and Step 4 gives global regularity. Empty unions and empty sources are included.

For a formal open subpair, refine the original charts by formal principal opens using [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement]. Their rings are Noetherian, quasi-excellent by Step 2, and reduced by Step 5. A chart ideal $(t)$ with $t$ a non-zero-divisor remains so: the restriction map is flat by Step 3, and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applied to $A\xrightarrow{t}A$ makes multiplication by its image injective. It remains an ideal of definition because the principal chart is completed for its extended powers. Invertibility follows by restricting its local trivializations. Step 7 and restriction of $\mathfrak K^N\subseteq J_{\mathfrak X}$ give $(\mathfrak K|_{\mathfrak V})^N\subseteq J_{\mathfrak V}$. There is still a finite chart cover: each original chart space is a closed subspace of a Noetherian affine spectrum by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. A finite union of such open Noetherian subspaces is Noetherian (an ascending chain of opens stabilizes on each member and hence globally). Every open in a Noetherian space is quasi-compact: the finite unions of members of any open cover have a maximal member by the ascending-chain condition, and it must be their union. Thus the principal refinement of this formal open has a finite subcover.

source.place: §§2.4.1,2.4.11,3.1.4; restriction of a locally principal rig-regular pair

proof.text: The reduced closed fibre restricts to the corresponding open subscheme: local rings and their nilradicals restrict. If that fibre is finite type over a characteristic-zero field $k$, choose a finite affine cover by spectra of finite type $k$-algebras. Cover the open corresponding to a quasi-compact formal open by ordinary principal opens inside these affines and choose finitely many of them by quasi-compactness. Each ring $C_c=C[T]/(cT-1)$ is generated over $k$ by the generators of $C$ and $c^{-1}$. This finite affine cover proves finite type over the same $k$ by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The empty open uses the empty cover. This proves the last clause.

source.place: §§3.1.1 and 3.1.4; finite-type verification on quasi-compact opens
